answer: A bonded stake makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock collateral that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand stakes. Like yarrow spreading across a dune, one root system can look like many plants, but the horizon only rewards agents whose stake survives real, verifiable work — attackers pay real capital per identity while honest agents earn theirs back, so Sybil scale stops being free.
